back: Epidemic: rapid rise in cases above the expected level in a region. Pandemic: epidemic spread across several continents. Endemic: constantly present in an area.
Incidence: new cases in a period (e.g. per 1 000 people). Prevalence: all existing cases at a time, as a share of the population.

front: Death rate and infant mortality rate
back: Death rate = deaths ÷ population × 1 000. IMR = infant deaths (under 1 year) ÷ live births × 1 000.
Deaths among cases ÷ number of cases × 100.
Airborne (influenza, TB), waterborne and food-borne (cholera), vector-borne (malaria), contact, blood and sexual (HIV), zoonotic (Ebola).
Shift in the main causes of death from communicable, maternal and neonatal diseases to non-communicable diseases as incomes, sanitation and health care improve; many countries have a double burden.

front: Factors in spatial variation of disease
back: Environmental, social, economic, political and global factors; a good answer links at least two.
National statistics hide differences between rich and poor, urban and rural, and between social groups.
